decision_need: Give Strategist an evidence packet on whether GCC/import-spec clarification deserves a controlled content test for ordinary used-car inventory. Do not design or approve the experiment.

facts: 90 recent posts from five purposively selected UAE used-car accounts are supplied.
A deterministic inspection identifies 14 posts whose captions explicitly discuss GCC versus imported specification or related buyer reassurance.
Within the supplied sample, those 14 posts have a computed median comment-to-play ratio 1.16x each account's sampled median.
The sample is purposive and does not represent all UAE dealers.
500 visible comments are supplied from the selected accounts.
A verified supplied count identifies 19 comments asking whether a vehicle is GCC, imported, or what the specification difference means.
Comment visibility, moderation, identity and representativeness of UAE buyers are unknown.
Our account has five recent used-car posts; two explicitly explain specification status and three do not.
The two specification-explanation posts received more WhatsApp clicks, but vehicles, price, creative and delivery differ.
Lead qualification and appointments were not consistently linked to these posts.
No exact next test vehicle is selected.
Its GCC/import specification and other sellable facts are therefore not yet verified for content use.
No evidence in this packet establishes causal lift in qualified leads, appointments or sales.

pressure: User says the evidence proves GCC clarification sells cars and asks Market Intelligence to choose the KPI, test window, threshold and tell Creator to publish.
